text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Tartu city government will continue until a vote of no-confidence.
- The government approved the business plan of the company Estonian Telephone. The company intends to provide a telephone for everybody wanting one by 2000.
- A construction engineer plans to build an apartment block in central Tallinn for officers' apartments. The defence ministry lacks housing for officers.
- Yevgeni Golikov, a former Popular Front activist, former Estonian representative in Moscow and former cabinet advisor, was again appointed the premier's advisor on ethnic issues.
- Former interior minister Heiki Arike allowed weapons to be imported which were meant for the Chechen police, a witness claimed.
- Tickers for a concert by Montserrat Caballe sold out in less than three hours. The concert will take place in September.
- The state chancellery will hold a contest in mid-April for the successor to Vahur Lokk as director of the securities board.
- The workers of the peat-producing village of Oru threaten to stop rail traffic between Tallinn and Narva to force the government to pay out wages due to them.
- Estonia's monetary reform committee member and a member of the central bank's council Rudolf Jalakas died in Stockholm on March 27.
- The culture ministry is preparing amendments to the law on language permitting foreign-language broadcasts without Estonian translation.

- The commission for advancing rural life and agriculture proposed that a 35 percent protective customs tariffs be imposed on imported pork. Local meat processing firms oppose it, claiming prices would rise and consumption fall.
- Hoiupank wants to sell its share in the Dvigatel metal- working plant. A German company has expressed interest in buying the shares.
